summary: Four studies directly apply graph neural network (GNN) message‑passing architectures to protein molecular function prediction. The most recent and highest‑performing is Gupta et al. (2024) [V0145], which uses a relational‑graph message‑passing network on the ProtMap dataset and attains 0.92 accuracy. Brennan et al. (2018) [V0148] applies the same GNN paradigm to MetroFlow, reporting an F1 score of 0.78. Haddad et al. (2025) [V0146] evaluates a relational‑graph GNN on FireScope and achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.64. Adebayo et al. (2026) [V0147] also uses relational‑graph message passing on the ChurnBench dataset, yielding an AUROC of 0.71. A fifth study, Duarte et al. (2020) [V0156], predicts protein molecular function with a decentralised training approach (not a GNN) and reports MAE = 0.65; it is included for completeness but does not meet the direct GNN criterion.
